working: 2,2-Dimethylcyclopentanone has α-H only at C-5. Crossed aldol with PhCHO gives the 5-benzylidene ketone. Both geometric isomers (E and Z, options 2 and 4) are possible products, though E is favoured. Self-aldol occurs when the C-5 enolate attacks a second ketone. Normal E1cB dehydration removes the α-H at C-5, giving the exocyclic, conjugated α,β-unsaturated product (option 3). Option 1 has its C=C inside the second ring, away from the carbonyl, so it is β,γ-unsaturated and unconjugated. That is not a product of aldol condensation. Option 4 (the Z-isomer) is the competing reading if 'cannot' means geometrically disfavoured.
